title: R Draconis — a pulsating giant star
status: measured; no change confirmed by our pre-set rule
plain_result: R Draconis is so bright that only the halo around its overloaded centre can be measured, and the pre-set test could use only three noisy colour bands: there no change passes 5 times the error (43 ordinary bright stars measured the same way). Shown for information only, outside the pre-set range: at 4.7 µm its brightness rises and falls by about 0.3 magnitudes either side of average and peaks around 1 Feb 2026 (± 3 days, formal). The catalogue predicts a visible-light maximum near 21 Jan 2026, uncertain by 2–3 weeks, so the infrared–visible lag is not measured.

method_note: Halo photometry (annulus 7–12 pixels) chosen on comparison stars before R Draconis was measured (docs/protocols/E9.md). Detectors 5–6 are excluded by a pre-set saturation guard; the 4.4–5 µm light curve was made after the result with that guard switched off, so it is descriptive. Published infrared maxima of such stars lag the visible ones by about 0.05–0.13 of a period, 12–32 days for R Draconis (Smith et al. 2002).
